text:
maria: quick heads-up — ran a regional benchmark sweep for the new 30B quantized build (int4) across us-west1 and eu-west1. attaching rough numbers and a proposed capacity plan. <https://internal.redwood/graphs/30b-int4/eu-us-latency.png>

jake: nice, can you paste the p50/p95 and throughput per GPU?

maria: p50: us-west1 18ms, eu-west1 23ms. p95: us-west1 120ms, eu-west1 165ms. tokens/s per gtx-rtx-class GPU: ~420 tok/s (us), ~390 tok/s (eu). results are with batching target 8 and kv-prefetch enabled.

priya: those p95 gaps are bigger than I'd expect. were kernel variants the same? (fused-attn vs cutlass/fp16 fallback)

maria: good call — I ran three kernel configs:
```
- fused-attn (recommended)
- cutlass fallback (fp16 paths)
- triton-slice (experimental, higher mem)
```

fused-attn gave best p50/p95 in us-west1, triton-slice had higher memory but lower p95 on eu when sequence len <=512. cutlass had slightly worse p50 but more stable tail for long seqs.

sam: for capacity planning, what's our target concurrency per GPU? previous plans used concurrency 10 for 30B fp16. int4 should be cheaper but sometimes CPU overhead for dequant hurts throughput.

maria: empirically with int4 and batching=8, stable concurrency is 6-9 depending on kernel. for safe SLO (p95 <200ms) I recommend targeting concurrency 7 and allowing autoscale headroom of 30% during regional peaks.

kevin: 30% headroom seems conservative. any sim data for 20% vs 30% on cost impact?

maria: yes — ran a quick sim for EU peak pattern (60m spike):
- 20% headroom: risk of breaches ~12% of minutes, cost baseline x1.0
- 30% headroom: risk <2%, cost ~x1.07
link to sim: <https://internal.redwood/sims/30b-headroom-eu.csv>

priya: sounds reasonable. can we mitigate with routing policy to burst to us-west in transient overloads? how about data residency concerns?

maria: we can route non-EU-regulated requests to us-west for spillover. for EU regulated data we keep within eu-west and increase dedicated pool target by +2 GPUs during business hours.

sam: operationally, what's the autoscaler config you used? paste snippet pls.

maria: config I tested: 
```
autoscaler:
  min_replicas: 4
  target_concurrency_per_gpu: 7
  scale_up_cooldown_sec: 60
  scale_down_cooldown_sec: 300
  headroom_pct: 30
```

kevin: ack. we should also include a fallback model (smaller 13B quant) in the rollout to guarantee availability if we hit capacity limits. Canary policy?

maria: agreed. propose canary route: 10% traffic to 13B-quant during peak windows, automatic rollback if quality drop >3% on eval set. eval hook: <https://internal.redwood/evals/30b-regression-suite>

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: dedicated-pool-eu-west1 scale-config update by maria at 2026-03-19T17:12:30Z :white_check_mark:

jake: cool. next steps: 1) update Dedicated pool target per region (eu +2 GPUs business hours), 2) set autoscaler as above, 3) add canary 13B route + eval guardrails, 4) run 48h soak and report back. anyone object?

priya: no objections. can you add the specific GPU types to the plan? (A10G vs A100 mix matters for kernel choice)

maria: plan uses A10G primarily in eu-west (cost preferred), A100s in us-west for peak throughput. kernel behavior: fused-attn tuned on A100s, fallback to cutlass on A10G. I'll drop a short doc with perf knobs.

kevin: thanks — if soak looks good we can move to reserve commit for eu pool next week. :thumbsup: 

maria: will run soak starting tomorrow and post updated charts in this thread.
